newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan new-crop cotton rises, old ends steady.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan new-crop cotton rises, old ends steady.

text.p: Pakistani new-crop cotton prices rose on Saturday on spinners' demand and good quality while the old-crop cotton ended steady in dull business, dealers at the private Karachi Cotton Association (KCA) said.
Higher buying propelled the price of the new (1997/98 July-June) crop cotton, dealer Nasim Usman said. "The new-crop cotton is particularly good for producing good-quality yarn."
Old-crop cotton ended steady amid small buying by exporters, Usman said. In the kerb market, the new-crop NIAB-78 variety was quoted from 2,550 to 2,560 rupees per maund (37.32 kg).
